newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Hekmatyar denies joining anti-Taleban alliance.
newsitem.headline: Hekmatyar denies joining anti-Taleban alliance.

text.p: Afghan faction leader Gulbuddin Hekmatyar said on Thursday he had not yet joined an alliance opposed to the Taleban militia, an Afghan news service said.
The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted a statement from Hekmatyar as saying reports of his joining the alliance were "premature", but that he was in talks with its members.

On Wednesday, sources close to Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum told AIP that Hekmatyar had decided at a meeting in the northern Afghan city of Mazar-i-Sharif to join the alliance grouping Dostum and ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani.
Hekmatyar, leader of the Hezb-i-Islami faction, was prime minister in Rabbani's government when the radical Islamic Taleban militia drove it out of Kabul on September 27.
Hekmatyar, who fled to the north after the fall of Kabul, stayed out of an anti-Taleban alliance that was formed between Dostum and Rabbani's military commander Ahmad Shah Masood.

The Taleban, who control at least two-thirds of Afghanistan, say Rabbani's government no longer exists and have demanded international recognition for their administration, which aims to spread strict Islamic sharia law throughout the country.
